title: The Gelin–Cesàro Identity via Catalan's Identity

problemStatement.plain: The Gelin–Cesàro identity: the product of the four Fibonacci numbers symmetrically flanking F(n) (two on each side) equals F(n)⁴ − 1. This open question asks to derive it from Catalan's identity F(m+r)² − F(m)·F(m+2r) = (−1)ᵐ·F(r)², already proved as fib_catalan_gap in the sibling entry fibonacci-identities-oq-01-oq-02-oq-01.
whyMatters: Shows the classical higher-degree Fibonacci product identities are not independent facts but structured products of the quadratic Catalan slices.
The difference-of-squares pattern (outer pair × inner pair with opposite signs) is a reusable template for wider symmetric flanking products F(n−k)·…·F(n+k).
Mathlib has no Fibonacci product identities of this degree, so the gap engine fib_gelin_cesaro_gap is an original contribution.

currentState.focus: SOLVED. Full verified proof (0 sorries, 0 axioms) plus gallery integration.
currentState.nextAction: Done. Optional follow-ups: generalise to 2k-term flanking products; Lucas-number analogue.

proven: fib_outer_pair / fib_inner_pair: the r=2 and r=1 Catalan slices, F(m)·F(m+4) = F(m+2)² − (−1)ᵐ and F(m+1)·F(m+3) = F(m+2)² + (−1)ᵐ.
Dependency fib_catalan_gap (Catalan's identity in gap form) from fibonacci-identities-oq-01-oq-02-oq-01, verified 0-axiom.
open: Generalise: is F(n−k)·…·F(n+k) always a polynomial in F(n) with constant term ±1, iterating the difference-of-squares pattern?
Lucas-number analogue via the Lucas Catalan identity.
